chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace: 'That Ali (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of'

a man who bought from another man a skin containing ghee, which had been hoarded as a single unit, and found in it butter. He disputed with him and went to Ali (peace be upon him). Ali (peace be upon him) said to him, 'For you is the amount of ghee corresponding to the measure of the butter.' The man said to him, 'I sold it to you as a hoarded unit.' Ali (peace be upon him) said to him, 'You bought ghee from him, and did not buy butter from him.'

key_terms.حُكْرَة: Hoarding or buying in bulk as a single unit
key_terms.رُبّ: Butter (often implying the solid part or a different quality than ghee)
key_terms.عُكَّة: A skin bag used for storing ghee or oil

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on selling a container with its contents as a single unit?
ai.summary: This ruling from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of distinguishing between the primary commodity (ghee) and its incidental byproduct (butter) in sales contracts, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding *'uyub* (defects). Imam Ali’s decision highlights the importance of precise intent (*niyyah*) and the specific terms of the agreement, ensuring that buyers are not penalized for natural variations in the product they did not explicitly purchase. This case underscores the practical application of fairness in commercial transactions within the Shia legal tradition.
